claims.text: Resistance to simultaneous wear and corrosion in high-entropy alloys is governed by a continuous, dense, adherent oxide film.
Surface enrichment of reactive elements such as Al, Cr, and Ti generates the protective oxide film in situ.
The initial AlCoCrFeNiTi- or MgAlTiVFeCo-type alloy has a homogeneous BCC or dual-phase microstructure.
The initial alloy surface is not yet passivated by an oxide layer.
High-temperature processing or controlled exposure selectively enriches reactive elements at the surface and promotes an adherent oxide film.
The proposed oxide film remains stable from room temperature to moderately elevated temperatures.
The structural mediator can be a dense, continuous spinel-type oxide or silicide-related layer.
A passive surface film reduces electrochemical dissolution and corrosion current.
The oxide film changes corrosion from direct metal attack to a diffusion-controlled mechanism.
The oxide film increases surface hardness and thereby reduces mechanical removal of the substrate.
A high-temperature, film-promoting treatment will produce a lower corrosion current density than a lower-temperature treatment of the same alloy.
An alloy bearing the in-situ film will have lower wear volume than a compositionally matched alloy without the film.
The protective film will reduce total material degradation during simultaneous wear and corrosion.
A lower-temperature or otherwise differently processed baseline will lack a significant protective oxide film.
The baseline will undergo direct solution attack and pitting together with higher abrasive wear.
The mechanism requires a sufficient fraction of reactive alloying elements and an environment that supports stable oxide formation.
Severe mechanical impact can disrupt film adhesion and cause the protection mechanism to fail.
The mechanism will fail in environments that dissolve the film or prevent a continuous film from forming.
The relative chemical-passivation and mechanical-barrier contributions vary with composition, processing history, and test conditions.
